## Runway

Runway is a self-hosted personal finance app: a Python backend in `runway/` (the HTTP handlers and the MCP server in `server/`, what Runway works out from your data in `domain/`, the outside services in `providers/`, the database in `storage/`), a Svelte web app in `frontend/`, a browser extension in `extension/`, backend tests in `tests/` (run with `unittest`) and the documentation site in `docs/`. It holds bank access and financial history, so a change to sign-in, the app lock, encryption, backups or anything that handles bank credentials is read against `SECURITY.md` as well as `AGENTS.md`.

## Private data here

The repository is public. Private data is anything read from a real instance: balances, amounts, merchants or payees, account and card names, lenders, budgets, income, dates of real transactions and people's names. It would land in tests, fixtures, screenshots and other images, docs, code comments, commit messages and pull request descriptions. Everything committed uses made-up figures and names: `tests/` builds its cases from `tests/forecast_support.py`'s `card_setup` and the helpers in `tests/shared.py`, and the demo data every screenshot shows is `runway/domain/demo.py`. Anything that looks like a real instance's figures, names or dates rather than that demo data is a blocking finding ("Personal financial data in the repo").

## Generated files and the checks that cover them

`docs/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/lib/api-types.ts` are the API contract (`make api-contract`, checked by `make api-contract-check` and `tests/test_api_contract.py`); `docs/feature-map.json` and the Feature map page `docs/src/content/docs/contributing/feature-map.md` are the feature map (`make feature-map`, checked by `make feature-map-check`); `tests/fixtures/forecast_golden.json` is the forecast's golden fixture (`tests/test_forecast_golden.py` fails when the forecast's results move). They are left out of the diff and listed in `omitted.txt`, with the lockfiles and the images. Don't spend time on their content, but flag one that looks stale beside its source in the diff: a changed route, contract type or test with no change to the generated file that should follow it, or the other way round; a lockfile that changes with no matching change to `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`. A changed golden fixture means the forecast's results changed: check the diff explains why.

## Where to look

`AGENTS.md`'s "Conventions" (the one paved path for each thing: HTTP only through `tls.urlopen`, request bodies through `runway/validate.py`, the half cent as `money.CENT`, no bare `date.today()` in sync and provider modules, `fetch(` only in `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, migrations with their own test) and "Mistakes that keep coming back" are the standard. Correctness first: money and date arithmetic, failure paths (what the user sees when it fails, stale state that says things are fine), races, data loss, migrations that can't run or go back. Then security and privacy: sessions, grants, tokens and keys that outlive their owner (`oidc.access_lapsed`), secrets, injection, and private data in logs and error reports (`monitoring.scrub`). Then tests: a behaviour change without a test, a skipped, weakened or deleted test, a test that writes to the shared database without `tests/shared.py`'s `own_database`. A change users or contributors would notice updates its page under `docs/src/content/docs/` in the same pull request, and a UI change commits the screenshots `make screenshots` writes to `screenshots/` (demo data only), never images copied in by hand.
